title: Adaptive stream windowing and idempotent retry patterns for Python SDK streaming chat
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Context:
Redwood's Python SDK streaming APIs work well for simple chat use-cases but teams building higher-throughput or multi-consumer consumers face two UX and correctness gaps: (1) backpressure/windowing ergonomics to avoid memory blowups and to give developers deterministic chunk semantics, and (2) idempotent retry semantics for client-initiated reconnects and server restarts so duplicate partial events don't produce inconsistent application state.

Goal:
Provide a minimal, ergonomic surface on the Python SDK that: (a) exposes an adaptive windowing API for streaming chat completions that batches events into developer-friendly chunks (tokens/messages/semantic frames), (b) provides built-in client-side idempotency and checkpoint tokens so reconnects can resume without duplication, and (c) ships examples and tests demonstrating migration from current iterator-based approach.

Design proposal (high level):
- Streaming primitives: introduce StreamWindow (configurable by max_tokens, max_time_ms, max_events) returned by high-level helper streamers. Default will be conservative: max_tokens=256, max_time_ms=150, max_events=8.
- Checkpointing: server emits checkpoint_id fields periodically. Client SDK persists last_checkpoint per stream and uses it on reconnect request as resume_checkpoint. Server will respond with delta events from that checkpoint.
- Idempotency: each client session attaches a client_stream_id (UUID v4) and optional operation_id for dedup at application level. SDK will automatically surface duplicate-suppression wrapper that drops events already seen per checkpoint window.
- Retry/backoff: built-in retry strategy for transient network errors with exponential backoff and jitter. Retries are safe because of checkpoint+idempotency contract. Provide opt-out for strict at-most-once users.
- Ergonomics surface: high-level API:
  - Chat.stream_with_windows(prompt, window_config=None) -> context manager yielding StreamWindow objects
  - StreamWindow.next_chunk() -> ChatChunk (chunk_type: [partial, message, done], tokens: str, tokens_count: int, checkpoint_id: str|None)
  - Low level fallback: Chat.raw_event_iterator() still available for advanced users

API examples (Python):
- High-level usage:
  with client.chat.stream_with_windows(prompt) as stream:
      for chunk in stream:
          if chunk.chunk_type == 'partial':
              render_partial(chunk.tokens)
          elif chunk.chunk_type == 'message':
              commit_message(chunk.tokens)
              persist_checkpoint(chunk.checkpoint_id)

- Resuming after a transient disconnect:
  last_checkpoint = load_checkpoint_from_store(session_id)
  with client.chat.stream_with_windows(prompt, resume_checkpoint=last_checkpoint) as stream:
      for chunk in stream:
          if chunk.checkpoint_id and chunk.checkpoint_id != last_checkpoint:
              apply_delta(chunk.tokens)

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- Server changes required: periodic checkpoint_id emission and resume endpoint support. Work with runtime team for lightweight proof-of-concept API changes. See runtime design doc link in updates.
- Memory/backpressure trade-offs: adaptive windowing grows on bursty input but bounded by max_tokens/event configuration. We choose defaults that favor latency-sensitive apps.
- Correctness: duplication suppression relies on deterministic checkpoint semantics. If server drifts, customers will observe missing/doubled tokens; plan to add telemetry to detect mismatches and fallback to raw_event_iterator.
- Complexity: keep high-level API conservative and implement complex behaviors only in the lower-level iterator to avoid surprising application behavior.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for windowing thresholds, time-based flush, and event boundaries.
- Integration tests with test runtime injecting disconnects and verifying no duplicate committed messages when using resume_checkpoint.
- Load test to validate memory bounds under bursty traffic (simulate 5k concurrent streams).

Migration guide for customers:
- Provide a short example converting from for-event-in stream() pattern to stream_with_windows() (one-page doc).
- Release notes highlighting: default behavior is opt-in; existing apps keep current behavior unless they upgrade to helper.

Acceptance criteria:
- API implemented and documented in sdk/python reference
- End-to-end integration test demonstrating resume with no duplicates
- Two example notebooks: small chat app and multi-consumer fanout example
- Perf regression < 8% p50 latency for typical small prompts compared to raw iterator

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Should we expose window metrics (flush_count, avg_window_tokens) via per-stream tracing? (proposal: yes, incrementally add to tracing schema)
- How aggressive should server-side checkpoint cadence be for high-throughput streams? (runtime team input needed)
